Keep frozen technical baseline `host_godot_boot` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

task_specification.objective: Deliver a closure-ready terminal celebration, a representative native-renderer dense-run profile, and a complete ordinary seven-to-ten-minute title-to-result run while preserving the verified animation, crowd, upgrade, shell, and restart foundations.

diagnosis.root_cause: Release convergence is blocked by two localized terminal-presentation defects plus two evidence gaps, not by a broken gameplay foundation. Bellkeeper defeat writes an absolute scale roughly 56 times its authored X/Z scale, obscuring the victory hold; victory audio is explicitly mapped to the same generic jump family used by movement feedback. The seven semantic Warden mappings, terminal lease, 40-actor bounded crowd systems, upgrade transaction, and product shell already exist, but ordinary-route victory ownership remains unverified because prior capture stopped in Wave 1, while performance was measured only under llvmpipe and therefore cannot qualify native 1920x1080 play.

stop_conditions: Do not replace or retune the preserved seven Warden semantic mappings, 40-actor pool, four-role roster, bounded neighbor and telegraph systems, authoritative upgrade transaction, or authored shell unless new candidate-bound evidence identifies a directly related defect.
Do not treat diagnostic victory or final-profile fixtures as proof of the ordinary route; keep preparation and advancement separate, editor-only, receipt-bearing, and unavailable in release exports.

If only llvmpipe or another software renderer is available, complete candidate repairs and performance observability but stop short of claiming native performance qualification; the host and Tester own that recapture and verdict.

If a bounded role session cannot observe the full 420–600 second route, do not add a shortcut that masquerades as ordinary completion. Preserve the natural route and hand the long-run capture to validation.
Do not schedule blocked backlog gaps, unrelated asset replacement, decorative expansion, host evidence generation, formal issue closure, or phase closure in this iteration.
Stop after the three selected surfaces pass focused Developer self-validation without fatal Godot/GDScript errors; formal check and issue disposition remain with GameLoop Runtime and Tester.

strategy.rationale: Change strategy from repeated animation-binding treatment to three independent root-cause passes: restore or retire the Bellkeeper instance relative to its authored scale and give victory a dedicated semantic audio family; preserve the proven Cheer mapping while binding its evidence to the real ordinary boss-defeat transaction; profile and optimize only measured dense-run hotspots on a representative native renderer; then tune and exercise the natural five-wave lifecycle and build paths instead of extending diagnostic selectors.

code: Run validate:native_godot_project and validate:host_godot_boot after candidate changes; require successful import/launch and no fatal GDScript or resource-load errors.
Inspect the final audio library binding to confirm victory resources are distinct from dash, jump and pickup mappings, have bounded playback ownership, and are covered by candidate provenance.
Verify every tester/validation InputMap action is created only under the editor feature guard and is absent from release exports.
Compare three post-reset lifecycle snapshots for stable pool size, actor/projectile/pickup/voice counts, signal ownership, pause state and run generations.
runtime: GameLoop Runtime and Tester rerun validate:release_convergence_animation_vfx_lighting_audio_contract using split victory prepare/advance for focused onset and audio capture, then an ordinary five-wave victory for authoritative Cheer, Result and Retry evidence.

Capture Master and Effects around terminal ownership acquisition at representative density; require one dedicated victory source event, no jump/dash-family resource, bounded duration, audibility, and retirement on Result, Retry and Title.

Rerun validate:release_convergence_dense_run_performance_contract at 1920×1080 on a recorded non-software renderer, sampling the representative final wave and three complete profile/reset cycles; llvmpipe measurements remain collector-only.

Rerun validate:release_convergence_complete_run_release_contract through one ordinary 420–600 second victory route, one ordinary failure route, clean Retry and Title return, plus separate natural runs demonstrating the three build shapes and truthful Result fields defensibly bound to runtime state.
visual: Capture Bellkeeper victory onset, approximately 0.9-second held Cheer, late hold/recovery, and Result handoff from identical shipped-camera framing; the Warden, Cheer motion, arena and escape lanes must remain readable throughout.

Capture representative native-renderer dense combat with 25–40 ordinary enemies, Bellkeeper, all weapon families, pickups, hostile telegraphs, HUD and boss health visible; compare the same framing before and after any hotspot repair.

Capture ordinary Title, active Wave 1, a three-card Draft, mixed-archetype Wave 4, Bellkeeper Wave 5, victory Result, failure Result, and clean Retry states, using the minimum distinct views needed to prove the complete lifecycle.

done_when: Bellkeeper defeat feedback uses its authored presentation scale as the reference—never the current absolute 1.4 X/Z target—and either remains bounded near that scale or retires before it can obscure the victory hold.

From the shipped high-angle camera, victory onset, the approximately 0.9-second held-Cheer frame, recovery, and Result handoff keep the Warden, authored Cheer, nearby arena, and useful escape lanes readable; no boss geometry covers most of the framebuffer.

Victory emits exactly one intentional, bounded cue from a dedicated semantic family that is not shared with dash, jump, pickup, or generic movement feedback; its source event remains audible at representative density and no terminal voice survives Result, Retry, or Title.

The real Bellkeeper defeated signal in an ordinary route records all five expected wave ids, diagnostic_jump_count 0, semantic state victory resolved to Cheer, one terminal lease owned by the run controller for the same run serial, exactly one Result commit, and Retry restoration to authored Idle with cleared terminal ownership.

The existing seven distinct deformation-bearing semantic mappings remain valid, including victory to Cheer; diagnostic victory receipts remain explicitly distinguishable from ordinary_victory_receipt and cannot satisfy ordinary-route acceptance.
Boss phase behavior, attack telegraphs, vulnerable recovery, result statistics, and failure/death terminal ownership remain unchanged outside the bounded victory repair.
tasks.instructions: Repair the terminal celebration as one event-owned presentation transaction. Replace the Bellkeeper's absolute death-scale expansion with direct authored-instance restoration, a scale-relative bounded effect, or early retirement before the hold; do not compensate through camera movement or Warden transforms. Audition and bind a licensed candidate-owned victory cue selected for celebratory identity and bounded duration, without reusing the jump/dash family or replacing otherwise working audio sources. Preserve the verified Warden animation profile and terminal lease implementation; for the repeated animation evidence issue, change only ordinary-route transaction binding or observability needed to prove that the actual five-wave Bellkeeper defeat owns Cheer, the single Result commit, and Retry-to-Idle reset. Keep split editor-only prepare/advance fixtures for focused retest, but ensure their route_kind and receipts remain diagnostic.
tasks.title: Isolate and repair the Bellkeeper victory celebration

done_when: A representative final-wave profile runs at 1920×1080 with 25–40 ordinary enemies, the Bellkeeper, all three weapon families, pickups, authored animation, VFX, bounded lights, gameplay HUD, and mixed audio present simultaneously.

The profile reports the actual renderer identity, resolution, frame-time distribution, sample duration, active and pooled actors, role composition, projectiles, pickups, light and telegraph admissions, neighbor-query bounds, presentation-update budgets, audio voices, and lifecycle generation so native qualification cannot be confused with software-renderer collection.
